Initial and imaging assessments documented renal impairment and several comorbid scan/ECG findings; routine scan modality is unspecified.

limitations: Routine head/abdomen/chest scans have no stated acquisition modality; no assumption they were CT. Independent tests have no invented strict order. Dates, insulin-clearance measurements, HLA/proteomic tests, potassium/beta-blocker treatment, generic plasma exchange/immunosuppression or specific hormone agent not inferred.

Shared discussion suggests possible concurrent LADA in both patients; positive IA-2/GADA does not establish LADA. claims.text: After stopping insulin, oral linagliptin 5 mg daily plus dorzagliatin 75 mg twice daily improved fluctuations but hypoglycemia persisted. Linagliptin was then stopped and oral acarbose 50 mg three times daily added, stabilizing glucose at 6–15 mmol/L. Follow-up serum insulin/IAA fell; possible concurrent LADA remained unexcluded and further C-peptide/autoantibody monitoring was recommended. Hormone therapy was not initiated. No discharge date is supplied.

evidence.quote: As a result, the patient was diagnosed with EIAS, and insulin was discontinued.
Upon cessation of exogenous insulin, the two individuals described in this article experienced relief from nocturnal and fasting hypoglycemia; thus, hormone therapy was not initiated.
A hypoglycemic regimen of linagliptin tablets, 5 mg orally once daily, combined with dorzagliatin, 75 mg orally twice daily, was initiated.
As anticipated, overall glucose fluctuation improved. Nonetheless, episodes of hypoglycemia persisted.
Linagliptin was discontinued, and oral acarbose tablets were added at a dosage of 50 mg three times daily.
This adjustment stabilized glycemic control, with blood glucose levels ranging from 6 to 15 mmol/L.
Serial monitoring during follow-up demonstrated a progressive decrease in serum insulin and IAA levels
Therefore, the possibility of concurrent LADA cannot be excluded.
patient 1 was positive for IA-2, while patient 2 was positive for GADA
To confirm the diagnosis, long-term monitoring of C-peptide and autoantibody levels is necessary.
Follow-up of the two patients revealed that C-peptide levels did not decrease as rapidly as observed in LADA.
the follow-up data revealed that both patients’ ICPR had dramatically dropped from the starting levels, suggesting that the EIAS condition had improved.

limitations: Routine head/abdomen/chest scans have no stated acquisition modality; no assumption they were CT. Independent tests have no invented strict order. Dates, insulin-clearance measurements, HLA/proteomic tests, potassium/beta-blocker treatment, generic plasma exchange/immunosuppression or specific hormone agent not inferred.

Shared discussion suggests possible concurrent LADA in both patients; positive IA-2/GADA does not establish LADA. DKD attribution is documented; unallocated discussion ESRD-progression wording is not assigned to both individuals. Needle reuse/fat hyperplasia as EIAS mechanism is author speculation.
